cards.Q179310: Computing turns information into useful systems: people design programs, build hardware, and organize data to solve practical problems.
cards.Q339338: Endianness orders a number's bytes in memory: big-endian puts the most significant byte at the lowest address; little-endian puts it last.
cards.Q189401: Virtual memory translates program addresses into physical locations; separate processes can use identical addresses while accessing different memory pages.
cards.Q165596: A cache keeps copies of recently accessed data in faster storage, making repeated or nearby memory accesses quicker when cache hits occur.
cards.Q201339: Public-key cryptography pairs public and private keys. For encryption, a public key encrypts messages that its corresponding private key decrypts.
cards.Q623447: Diffie–Hellman lets two parties calculate the same shared secret by combining their private key with the other party's public key.
cards.Q264164: Recursion solves a problem through calls to the same function on smaller instances; a reachable base case stops the calls.
cards.Q2078: Standalone SVG describes vector shapes in XML text; the shapes can scale cleanly while text-based properties remain editable.
cards.Q245: Raspberry Pi computers connect software to hardware through configurable pins that programs can read as digital inputs or set as outputs.
cards.Q187899: Deep Blue searched chess positions in parallel, combining position evaluation with a database of grandmaster games to choose moves.
cards.local:authored:000574: Microeconomics studies choices by people and firms, such as what households buy and how businesses decide prices and production.
cards.Q215551: Comparative advantage means producing something at a lower opportunity cost: giving up less of another product, even without being the most productive.
cards.Q272458: Public goods are costly or impossible to exclude people from using, while one person's use does not reduce availability to others.
cards.Q5970087: Economies of scale occur when expanding production lowers average cost in the long run, when firms can change all their inputs.
cards.Q223639: Elasticity measures proportional responsiveness; price elasticity compares percentage changes in quantity demanded or supplied with percentage changes in price.
cards.Q382444: Marginal cost is the extra cost divided by extra output; average cost instead spreads total cost across all units produced.
cards.Q466764: Fixed costs stay unchanged as output varies in the short run; a signed factory lease is one example until it expires.
cards.Q806663: A bank run occurs when many depositors withdraw together; even a solvent bank can fail if it cannot turn assets into cash quickly.
cards.Q320863: The World Bank Group's five institutions support development through different tools, including lending to governments and investing in private businesses.
cards.local:authored:000545: Civil engineering designs and maintains infrastructure people share, such as bridges, transport routes, and systems that deliver clean drinking water.
cards.Q654051: A turbofan's fan sends air through an engine core and around it in a bypass stream; both streams contribute thrust.
cards.Q626658: Fly-by-wire sends pilot commands electrically to actuators that move aircraft control surfaces; digital systems use computers to replace direct mechanical linkages.
cards.Q12570: A suspension bridge hangs its deck from main cables through vertical hangers; at the Golden Gate, towers and anchorages carry the loads.
cards.Q1429218: Cantilever bridges extend arms from supporting towers or piers; at the Forth Bridge, suspended spans connect the projecting arms.
cards.Q190100: A bearing supports a moving part while carrying forces; rolling bearings place balls or rollers between rings to permit rotation.
cards.Q1934967: On a derailleur bicycle, shifting to a smaller front chainring or larger rear cog makes pedaling easier by changing the gearing.
cards.Q82412: Epicyclic gearing arranges planet gears around a sun gear; multiple planets share loads, helping a compact mechanism transmit substantial torque.
cards.Q2878855: Bus rapid transit combines dedicated bus lanes with features such as off-board fare collection and platform-level boarding to speed passenger service.
cards.Q40176: Singapore's MRT includes the North East Line, a fully automated underground heavy-rail line operating without drivers.
cards.Q274897: Portal turns paired gateways into puzzles: players and objects enter one opening and emerge from its linked partner.
cards.Q49740: Minecraft's Survival mode requires players to gather building materials; Creative mode supplies blocks directly, changing the constraints on what players can build.
cards.Q71910: Tetris pieces fall into a grid; fitting them into complete horizontal lines clears those lines and makes space for more pieces.
cards.Q138: Except when castling, a chess king moves one square in any direction, and cannot move to a square an opponent attacks.
cards.Q139: A chess queen moves any distance horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, but cannot jump over pieces in its path.
cards.Q165704: In high jump, athletes take off from one foot and try to clear an elevated horizontal bar without knocking it down.
cards.Q327742: In stadium relay races, teammates pass a baton; a legal exchange depends on the baton's position inside the takeover zone.
cards.Q187204: Triple jump combines hop, step, and jump: the hop lands on the takeoff foot, then the step lands on the opposite foot.
cards.Q136851: Curling players slide stones toward a target; rotation added at release influences which direction the stone curves.
cards.Q35395: Phonetics studies speech physically: how the body produces sounds and how sound-wave properties can be measured.
cards.Q43249: A morpheme is a smallest meaningful language unit: 'dogs' has two, 'dog' and plural '-s', although it has only one syllable.
cards.Q148877: In speech, assimilation makes one sound more like a neighboring sound; influence may come from the sound before or after it.
cards.Q208084: Grammatical aspect can present an event as ongoing or complete; tense instead locates it in time, such as past or present.
cards.Q255615: Code-switching alternates languages within a conversation or utterance; recognizing such speech requires handling more than one language in the same exchange.
cards.Q286576: Registers distinguish language by situation of use, such as conversation or research methods; dialects distinguish varieties associated with different speaker groups.
cards.Q5378197: English Braille represents writing with raised-dot cells; contracted forms use symbols for frequent words or letter groups instead of spelling every letter.
cards.Q14759: American Sign Language uses hands and facial movements with its own grammar; it differs from English and from other signed languages.
cards.local:authored:000685: In Montessori infant and toddler classrooms, children choose accessible materials, work with them, and return them before selecting another activity.
cards.Q212737: Classical conditioning links stimuli: after repeated tone-food pairings, Pavlov's dogs salivated to the tone, which previously had not triggered that response.
cards.Q847079: Operant conditioning changes behavior through consequences: reinforcement makes a behavior more likely, while punishment makes it less likely.
cards.Q272021: Gestalt psychology examines organized perception: dots close together tend to look like a group, showing how arrangement shapes what people perceive.
cards.Q783092: Executive functions are skills for managing tasks, such as focusing attention, planning ahead, and switching between demands.
cards.Q221284: Conformity means changing behavior to follow a group; people may do this to gain acceptance even when they privately disagree.
cards.Q191062: A mnemonic supplies cues for remembering: HOMES uses the initials of Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, and Superior to recall the Great Lakes.
cards.Q1377840: Forgetting can occur when memories interfere: older learning disrupts recall of newer information, or newer learning competes with an older memory.
cards.Q1860557: Self-concept is how someone thinks and feels about themselves; Carl Rogers distinguished a person's perceived real self from their ideal self.
cards.Q161272: Social psychology studies how other people and situations shape thoughts, feelings, and actions, considering both social circumstances and individual characteristics.
cards.Q841628: Social stratification ranks groups by resources and status; education, income, and family background can influence someone's position.
cards.Q194417: Social mobility changes someone's position in a class system; intergenerational comparisons track parents and children, while intragenerational comparisons follow one lifetime.
cards.Q741550: Cultural relativism interprets practices using a culture's own standards; understanding those practices does not require endorsing them.
cards.Q5446591: Fictive kinship creates recognized family ties through social relationships, without requiring shared ancestry; godparenthood is one example.
cards.Q1163216: In symbolic interactionism, people create meanings through interaction; valuing books can develop through shared reading routines with family or friends.
cards.Q185467: Socialization is lifelong learning of a group's norms and values; joining a new workplace can mean adapting to different expectations.
cards.local:authored:000032: Universal design aims for usability across diverse abilities, using features such as clear information and low physical effort in products and environments.
cards.Q461: Internet Archive's Wayback Machine preserves captured webpages for browsing by URL and date; missing captures can leave gaps in a site's history.
cards.Q740308: UNICEF supports childhood immunization by procuring cold-chain equipment that protects vaccines during storage and transport.
